title: R' Pinchas Dedehuva
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Kohelet Rabbah 2:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.2.2.4), Rabbi Pinchas Dedehuva says, “It is mixed—what joy does it produce?” Seder HaDorot holds that this is not the name of a city; rather, the reading should be “Rabbi Pinchas said: This laughter is mixed.”[^1]

[Vayikra Rabbah 20:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.20.3) similarly cites Rabbi Abba bar Kahana opening with “Of laughter I said, it is mad”: “If this laughter is mixed, what benefit does joy bring?” Hyman therefore calls the author of Sheva Chokhmot’s claim that it is the name of a city a mistake.[^2]

notes.text: Dedehuva is retained as a name-form without deciding that it is a place. The TE Kohelet Rabbah has Didhuba. Seder HaDorot’s proposed word division and the claim attributed to Sheva Chokhmot remain distinct from that reading.

The printed notice reads דחוכא, “laughter,” and ב״כ, Abba bar Kahana, where the accepted Hebrew transcription has דחובא and ב״ב. The TE Vayikra Rabbah likewise names Abba bar Kahana. “Mixed” is literal: the fuller story joins a wedding feast with a death. The corresponding passage is 20:3 in the linked edition.
